posts.title: VEON after earnings: is the debt story finally improving?
posts.text: Went through the VEON quarterly numbers. Revenue growth in local currency looks solid, but I still worry about the debt maturities over the next two years. Anyone modelled the refinancing?

posts.parent: VEON after earnings: is the debt story finally improving?
posts.text: Net debt is coming down but slowly. The leverage only looks fine if the currencies in Pakistan and Bangladesh hold, and that is a big if.

posts.title: $VEON looks undervalued versus other emerging market telcos
posts.text: At this multiple VEON stock is cheap compared with peers. The digital services revenue is growing fast and the market is not pricing it in. I added to my position.

posts.title: How exposed is VEON to Ukraine now that Kyivstar is listed separately?
posts.text: Trying to understand the geopolitical risk for VEON shareholders. Kyivstar is still a large part of the group. A bad turn in the war could hit the valuation hard.
The VEON buyback is welcome but small. I would rather they paid down debt first before returning cash to shareholders.

posts.title: VEON Q3 earnings review: growth, debt and what comes next
posts.text: A walk through the VEON Ltd quarterly results: revenue, EBITDA, the balance sheet and management guidance for the full year.

posts.parent: VEON Q3 earnings review: growth, debt and what comes next
posts.text: Good breakdown. Management guidance was raised again, which makes me more confident in holding the shares long term.

posts.parent: VEON Q3 earnings review: growth, debt and what comes next
posts.text: Nobody talks about the currency devaluation risk. Earnings in dollars could shrink quickly and the debt is in hard currency.

posts.parent: Is VEON stock a buy? Emerging market telecom deep dive
posts.text: I sold my VEON shares last month. The regulatory risk in those markets is too high for me and the stock has been dead money.

posts.title: Secure Trust Bank: how big is the motor finance redress risk?
posts.text: Secure Trust Bank shares have been weak since the FCA motor finance review. The provision they took looks small to me. Does anyone think the redress bill could be much larger?

posts.parent: Secure Trust Bank: how big is the motor finance redress risk?
posts.text: Vehicle finance is a meaningful part of the loan book, so I am cautious. Impairments were already rising before the FCA got involved.

posts.title: Secure Trust Bank trading below tangible book value
posts.text: Secure Trust Bank looks undervalued at this share price. Profit is growing, the dividend is covered and it trades at a discount to book. Small UK lenders are out of favour, which is the opportunity.

posts.title: Secure Trust Bank results: net interest margin holding up
posts.text: Read the Secure Trust Bank results. Net interest margin held up better than I expected and deposits grew. Cost of risk ticked up though, which is the thing to watch.

posts.title: Secure Trust Bank shares: cheap UK bank or value trap?
posts.text: Looking at Secure Trust Bank PLC: the retail finance and vehicle finance divisions, impairments, the dividend and the FCA motor finance review.

posts.parent: Secure Trust Bank shares: cheap UK bank or value trap?
posts.text: The dividend yield is attractive and earnings cover it comfortably. I have been buying the shares on weakness.

posts.parent: Secure Trust Bank shares: cheap UK bank or value trap?
posts.text: Value trap in my view. Arrears are climbing and the regulator is not finished with motor finance. I am staying away from the stock.

posts.title: Take-Two earnings: bookings guidance raised, GTA VI date unchanged
posts.text: Take-Two Interactive raised net bookings guidance and kept the GTA VI release window. The stock is up after hours. NBA 2K and mobile carried the quarter.

posts.parent: Take-Two earnings: bookings guidance raised, GTA VI date unchanged
posts.text: Everything about the TTWO valuation depends on GTA VI shipping on time. One more delay and the shares give back the whole year's gains.

posts.parent: Take-Two earnings: bookings guidance raised, GTA VI date unchanged
posts.text: Recurrent consumer spending keeps growing, which is what matters for margins. I think the market still underestimates how profitable the online mode will be.

posts.title: Is $TTWO overvalued ahead of GTA VI?
posts.text: The stock already prices in a huge launch. Development costs have ballooned and the P/E is stretched. I am worried there is more downside than upside from here for investors.

posts.title: GTA 6 trailer 3 breakdown: every detail you missed
posts.text: The map looks enormous and the lighting is incredible. Can't wait to play this, the vehicles and the wildlife look amazing.

posts.title: Take-Two Interactive Q2 earnings: what investors need to know
posts.text: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) reported results. We cover net bookings, guidance, the GTA VI timeline, development costs and what analysts are saying about the shares.

posts.parent: Take-Two Interactive Q2 earnings: what investors need to know
posts.text: Strong quarter. Guidance was raised and the balance sheet is fine. I am holding my shares through the launch.

posts.parent: Take-Two Interactive Q2 earnings: what investors need to know
posts.text: Layoffs at the studios while the CEO talks about record bookings is a bad look. Management credibility is an issue for me as an investor.

posts.parent: Take-Two Interactive Q2 earnings: what investors need to know
posts.text: If they price the game at $100 there will be a backlash, and that is a real risk to the revenue forecast analysts are using.
